title: HIT PARADE
short_description: HIT PARADE - a 3D versus fighting game staged as a late-night TV fight show. Twelve contestants, five condemned sets, an arcade season that ends against the host himself, local and online versus, and a full training room.
description:
LIVE ON KNOCKOUT 13.

Every Friday night an underground network takes over the airwaves with HIT PARADE, a no-rules fight show shot on condemned sets across a rotting city. Contestants sign up for money, revenge or fame. The cameras never cut away.

HIT PARADE is a 3D-rendered versus fighting game played on a single fight line, Street Fighter style: walk, dash, jump, crouch, block by holding back, and trade light, medium and heavy attacks plus a special button, throws, parries, IMPACT attacks, supers and a cinematic Level 3 super for every contestant.

THE CAST - twelve fighters:
- JOHNNY RIOT, the headliner boxer
- PATCH, the floor manager rushdown
- BRUNO "THE FRIDGE", an armored grappler
- THE GREAT ZAMBINI, a teleporting card-throwing zoner
- OFFICER KRANE, a charge fighter with a riot shield
- LOTUS LIU, a drunken-stance fighter
- BONEYARD, the butcher of Block Street
- SPIN, an aerial b-boy
- GAZZA, who fights with a football
- RERUN, the contestant who counters everything
- THE FREAK (mini boss) and RICKY MARQUEE, the host and final boss, who changes his act halfway through the fight. Clear THE SEASON to unlock both.

MODES:
- THE SEASON: an arcade ladder of 8 episodes against the CPU - random contestants, your rival, the mini boss and the host in his own control room. Two bonus rounds break it up: BRAWL BREAK (45 seconds against waves of studio goons) after episode 3 and HECKLER TOSS (40 seconds of parrying what the crowd throws) after episode 6. Continues, a closing story for every contestant and a local score board. THE PILOT is the short cut: 5 episodes with BRAWL BREAK after episode 2.
- VERSUS: two players on one screen, or you against the CPU at difficulty 1 to 8, on any of the five stages.
- ONLINE: quick match or a private four-letter room code, with rollback netcode.
- TRAINING: a dummy that stands, crouches, jumps, blocks or fights back as a CPU, 3-second record and playback, input display, frame data, hitboxes and every move list.

FIVE STAGES: The Rust Theater, Butcher Block, Wheel of Pain, Channel 13 Rooftop and The Control Room.

Two control types with the same timing underneath: SIMPLE (the special button plus a direction) and CLASSIC (motion inputs). Keyboard, gamepad and on-screen touch controls.

Comic violence only: hits land with a hard freeze and a red cartoon splash (or sparks, or confetti), never realistic gore.
controls_keyboard: P1: W A S D move, jump (W or SPACE) and crouch; hold back to block · J light · K medium · L heavy · I special · U assist (hold) · H throw · O parry · P impact · Y taunt · ESC pause. P2 on the same keyboard: arrow keys · Numpad 1 / 2 / 3 light / medium / heavy · Numpad 5 special · Numpad 4 assist · Numpad 0 throw · Numpad 6 parry · Numpad + impact · Numpad * taunt
controls_gamepad: Standard gamepad: left stick or d-pad move · X light · Y medium · RB heavy · A special · B assist (hold) · LT throw · LB parry · RT impact · SELECT taunt · START pause
art_direction: Key art for a late-night TV fight show, built as stylised 3D with cel-shaded characters and thick ink outlines. Two fighters square off on a condemned studio set: a lean boxer in taped fists and a sleeveless shirt throwing a straight right, and a huge slab of a grappler with a shaved head, arms wide, ready to grab. Blue-painted stone brick walls, iron-banded doors, harsh studio spotlights, a shadowy crowd behind a rope line, light haze. A red LIVE bug and a slanted yellow ratings frame suggest the broadcast without readable text. Saturated palette: ink purple-black #140d1f, signal red #ff2e4d, marquee yellow #ffd23a, cream #fff4e0. Punchy, comic energy with a motion-smear on the swing and a small cartoon impact star; no gore. No text, no logos, no ships, no pirates, no nautical props.
